verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.17
2. Lay Followers
The Builder

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṁ kārāpeti.
verses.english: Now at that time the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder was having some building work done in that jungle thicket.

verses.pali: Addasā kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ aññatarasmiṁ sālarukkhamūle nisinnaṁ pallaṅkaṁ ābhujitvā ujuṁ kāyaṁ paṇidhāya parimukhaṁ satiṁ upaṭṭhapetvā.
verses.english: He saw the Buddha sitting down cross-legged at the root of a certain sal tree, his body set straight, and mindfulness brought to the present.
Seeing this, it occurred to him,

verses.pali: “ahaṁ kho imasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe kammantaṁ kārāpento ramāmi.
verses.english: “I enjoy having this building work done here in the jungle.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ samaṇo gotamo kiṁ kārāpento ramatī”ti?
verses.english: I wonder what the ascetic Gotama enjoys having done?”

verses.pali: Atha kho navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then Bhāradvāja the Builder went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“What kind of works are done by you,
a mendicant in the sal jungle?
How do you find enjoyment
alone in the wilderness, Gotama?”
“There’s nothing I need do in the jungle;
my jungle’s cut at the root, it’s withered away.
Free of snarls and thorns in the jungle,
I enjoy solitude, having given up discontent.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, navakammikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Builder said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …

verses.pali: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
